note: Three accepted rail research publications as distinct typed evidence studies. They are not pooled with directed-rail-v3, they are not promises or certificates, and no research code runs as a product check.

review.note: Correction review requested; the corrected head was accepted after independent reproduction of all 43 tests and the three read-only checks.

rail-query-model-v1.scope: Query-scoped reachability: whether one exact selected literal Train request, between Outside positions on a saved export, is predicted to return a complete path within the 100000-unit bound. Fitted retrospectively; not a place-level promise, service claim or native junction law.
rail-query-model-v1.method: The accepted study froze its protocol and predictions before opening any observation, then scored the fitted straightest-continuation junction rule on the 276 selected literal-boundary native requests (32 stock control + 244 cohort). A read-only export bridge re-derives every model-used field from the saved CRP bytes and compares it with the native network snapshot. This ledger re-checks the archived bytes and recomputes every rate from the preserved counts.
rail-query-model-v1.limits: Already-observed retrospective fit on the 276 selected literal requests of the accepted native cohort, not a blind or prospective holdout. The junction family was chosen after the first family was scored, so the fitted rule is a hypothesis and not an accepted native rule. Every observed success sits inside one weak Train component and all 51 cross-component requests fail; that is a statement about this selected set, not a proof that a connection can never be joined. Native lane connectivity, junction behaviour, path cost and rejected pairs are inferred from outcomes. The 100000 length bound, the 128-request cap, Pittsburgh's 112 unqueried candidates, dynamic-assembly exclusion, plugins, three DLC-panel errors and Pittsburgh's separately audited degraded strict teardown bound the claim. FILE identity is not memory attestation or strict no-mods. Rail service, train spawning, editor/gameplay parity, sustained gameplay and human play are not verified. No geographic accuracy, prevalence, no-rail certificate, service or live yes is claimed.

export_bridge.scope: read the nine unchanged cohort packages and the two stock controls; never rebuild, recapture or repair
export_bridge.status_note: Every model-used field is readable from the saved export: segment identity, endpoints, prefab, node position, lane type/vehicle/category/direction and the Outside and Invert predicates. The prefab lane template and the flag-name tables are hash-bound observed catalogs rather than export bytes on their own, and both are cross-validated leave-one-package-out. Node OneWayIn/OneWayOut names are recomputed by the game at load and are not claimed as export bytes.

review.note: Independent PASS reproduced all 58 rules and 174 grouped rate tables and traced the retained successful Pittsburgh path.

rail-junction-fit-v1.scope: Export-tangent junction pairing: whether the straightest continuation measured from each segment's authored endpoint tangents pairs the lanes the game used. Export-derived hypothesis, fitted retrospectively; not native-attested and not a ruleset for product use.
rail-junction-fit-v1.method: The accepted study predeclared a closed set of junction pairings and a 0-180 degree grid, wrote features and predictions before opening any observation, and scored 58 rules on the same 276 requests. Its chord family is an independent reimplementation that reproduces the accepted predictions exactly. Grouped leave-one-package-out selection is applied to the nine cohort packages. This ledger re-checks the archived bytes, the accepted prefix hashes and the derived tables.
rail-junction-fit-v1.limits: Retrospective on an already-observed cohort, not a blind holdout. Tangent fields are not native-attested: the accepted native snapshots do not emit them, so every tangent value is read from the export and is an export-derived hypothesis. Strict leave-one-package-out selection picks the tangent rule in five of six cohort folds, but Pittsburgh, the only package that discriminates the rules, is the held-out fold where every remaining-perfect rule ties; the pooled selected out-of-fold result is therefore 10/4/229/1, identical to the reference, and neither number is a blind estimate. The false negative's native path is not reproduced by either rule (it crosses a pair both pairings reject), so the tangent rule matches the outcome through a different route: a better fit, not an identified junction law. The 100000 bound, the 128-request cap, Pittsburgh's 112 unqueried candidates, dynamic-assembly/plugin/DLC limits and Pittsburgh's degraded strict teardown bound the claim. No game, browser, server or rebuild; no old scorer rerun.

rail-stock-holdout-v1.scope: Frozen stock-package holdout: whether each frozen rule predicts the exact selected literal Train request result on packages selected before any new query. Request-scoped, not geographic prevalence, service, a junction law or a product promise.
rail-stock-holdout-v1.method: The pre-query freeze selected two pairing-difference, four same-pairing and four unsupported packages from the 102 non-control stock maps, fixed eight requests per supported package, and recorded both rules' predictions before any new native query. Twelve openings then ran the unchanged controls and the ten holdouts; the evaluator binds each request to its frozen prediction, the native result, the package bytes and the pre/post graph digests, reports the all-complete intent-to-test and the predeclared snapshot-matched tables, and keeps every unsupported or unqueried row explicit. This ledger re-checks every archived hash and recomputes both tables from the preserved rows.
rail-stock-holdout-v1.limits: A deterministic stock selection inside the old catalog's supported domain, not blind global accuracy or geographic prevalence. Both rules predicted the same answer for all 48 selected requests before any native query, so this selection has no power to prefer tangent over chord. The eight failures belong to one package and are not independent package-level votes; each failure labels only its exact request and protocol, never geographic absence, service, spawning, a product promise or a junction law. Four unsupported packages stay metadata-only with no requests; supported package coverage is 6/10 of the selected packages. The optional Pittsburgh replay was not run and the retained successful-path counterexample is unresolved. The three post-load errors and the dynamic-assembly exclusion stay recorded. FILE identity is not memory attestation or strict no-mods, and stock packages have no prepared-input or CPU receipt lineage.
